workshops.title: Build an auditable UI runtime and lifecycle notebook
workshops.summary: Use one standalone synthetic iOS target and shared host checks to connect observation, input routing, layer interruption, baseline/RTL layout, focus, routes, and expiring work.

sections.title: Build the companion at the boundary you can actually verify
sections.html:
Start with a scratch application rather than adapting the company client. UIRuntimeLab is an actual Xcode application project with a shared scheme, explicit Info.plist, registered custom URL scheme, iPhone/iPad destinations, and an iOS 17 deployment target. It uses Apple SDKs, synthetic strings, and no remote packages, credentials, signing team, or network operations. Swift 5 language mode is selected; the authoring compiler is Apple Swift 6.4. A compiler version and deployment target answer different questions.

Read the README's commands before executing them. Build output and module caches belong under the unique UIRuntimeLab-093-096-20261102 paths in /private/tmp. An ordinary simulator build failed because the compiler macro helper could not initialize its nested sandbox. The documented -Xfrontend -disable-sandbox flag allowed compilation inside the existing outer sandbox. This flag is an environment workaround on the command, not a checked-in change to production or a simulator runtime result.

The scheme creates a simulator application product. That is stronger than merely typechecking a detached function because the target's source list, entry point, plist, linking, and packaging participate. It still does not prove installed custom URL delivery, recognizer interaction, text measurement, VoiceOver announcement, two-window behavior, or background expiration. CoreSimulator was unavailable during authoring. Keep those acceptance rows pending rather than making up screenshots or completion claims.

Host checks compile the same shared FlowMath, LabRoute, and CounterRecord sources used by the app. Their exact outputs are recorded in the README. This establishes geometry/policy behavior and macOS KVO delivery at their real boundaries. It does not make the KVO script a UIKit app or the route reducer an operating-system link delivery test.

sections.title: Trace registration, hit selection, and action dispatch separately
sections.html:
The Routing tab hosts DispatchController through UIViewControllerRepresentable. Its CounterRecord is an NSObject with @objc dynamic count. viewWillAppear creates a retained observation using .initial and .new; viewDidDisappear invalidates it. The callback uses weak self and asserts main-thread execution because every writer in this demonstration is a UIKit action. Initial delivery occurs before registration returns, so the label is constructed before the controller starts observing.

The Increment button has an explicit target. Reset has a nil target and a compiler-checked selector implemented by the containing controller, so UIKit's responder-chain action resolution is exercised. A decorative PassThroughOverlay returns nil only when ordinary hit testing selected the wrapper itself. That permits the underlying controls to receive touches without relying on transparent pixel color. These are different mechanisms and need separate evidence rows.

The neighboring pad installs single and double tap recognizers. The single requires the double to fail. Record the actual action that fires and its synthetic count change. Do not remove the required delay with a timer or reverse the dependency. Leave and return to the tab to observe a fresh initial value without duplicate registrations. Essential count actions remain semantic buttons; the tap pad is only a diagnostic surface.

For an Android engineer, listener ownership, View dispatch, and interception provide useful questions, but they do not collapse into UIKit's KVO, responder, and recognizer contracts. The host KVO executable checks synchronous initial/new delivery and repeated invalidation. The UI notebook must additionally establish action routing and visible registration behavior on an identified destination.

sections.title: Retarget the layer while keeping a truthful model destination
sections.html:
The Layers tab owns a blue decorative CALayer in MovingLayerView. Move left or right first lays out the canvas, copies presentation position when available, and computes the endpoint. A transaction disables implicit actions, removes the owned travel key, writes the model destination, and adds a CABasicAnimation from the sample unless Reduce Motion is enabled. The last command therefore defines lasting state independently of how far the previous animation progressed.

Use the Sample button to inspect model and presentation values. Unavailable presentation is reported explicitly. A sample is not a synchronized display capture or timing trace. Press the opposite endpoint during motion and record whether retargeting appears continuous. Freeze captures a presentation sample before removing the animation and writes it back into the model. Removing the animation without that assignment would expose the endpoint instead.

Resize invokes the declared freeze-and-clamp policy. Leaving the controller freezes the decorative movement. No animation completion triggers a business operation, and no Task.sleep is used to wait for the animation. The one-and-a-half-second duration is a fixture parameter, not a measured frame budget. Keep the synthetic checkpoint sleep in the lifecycle surface conceptually separate from animation.

Android ObjectAnimator is a helpful comparison but can update a target property over time, whereas the Core Animation model already holds the endpoint. Record source/build evidence separately from rapid-retarget, freeze, resize, and Reduced Motion observations. Investigating commit-side versus render-side hitches needs a later trace workflow; this companion has no signpost distributions or claimed performance improvements.

sections.title: Run geometry checks, then inspect actual text and focus
sections.html:
FlowMath accepts measured sizes, first baselines, and break flags, then produces local logical origins for SwiftUI to place. BaselineFlow supplies those current values through SwiftUI subview proxies. Its signature includes normalized width, all ordered metrics and gaps. updateCache clears prior data; repeated probes also compare the signature. This conservatively caches arrangement while remeasuring child dimensions, so do not describe it as a proven text-measurement optimization.

The host fixture aligns a forty-by-twenty/baseline-fifteen child and a fifty-by-thirty/baseline-twenty child with origins y = five and zero. Their baseline is twenty and their row height thirty. At seventy-point width, they wrap with twelve points between rows and total height sixty-two. The logical x origins stay zero and forty-eight in both directions. SwiftUI automatically reflects subview x placement in RTL; the helper must not reflect first. A numeric anchor does not disable framework reflection, and host checks do not observe native RTL. Empty, zero-width, oversize, changed-metric, and forced-break inputs have explicit behavior.

The Layout tab supplies mixed fonts, a forced next-row key, an RTL fixture toggle, and an orthogonal nested horizontal scroller. It leaves native scroll arbitration intact. Name and Note have distinct FocusState cases; submit and keyboard toolbar actions request progression using current scroll IDs. A separate AccessibilityFocusState requests the visible validation error. These source affordances require runtime checks for actual keyboard and assistive behavior.

Change text size and width, inspect line wrapping and baseline agreement, then test diagonal scrolling, Previous/Next/Done, hardware traversal, and VoiceOver reading/activation. The same array order is retained under RTL; do not reverse semantic identity to repair geometry. The custom layout does not define an explicit outer first/last baseline guide and does not implement same-axis nested fling transfer. Mark those as further extensions rather than silently claiming platform parity.

sections.title: Exercise routing and bounded work without inventing durability
sections.html:
The app uses one UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor for process launch and a WindowGroup of scene roots. Each root reads its own scenePhase and stores a lightweight route ID with SceneStorage. Its NavigationStack path is derived from validated alpha/beta values. Incoming URLs use the same strict LabRoute parser as the host executable. Accepted warm input replaces selection; rejected warm input preserves it. The separate cold reducer establishes valid external intent over stale restoration and a safe-root policy for invalid incoming intent.

On a functioning runtime, install the built app, open uiruntime://item/alpha while running, terminate it, and open uiruntime://item/beta cold. Record actual delivery and presentation. On a platform supporting multiple windows, give each window a different selection and move only one through phase changes. A scene connection may restore a session; disconnection is not guaranteed session discard or process termination. Do not reconstruct a universal lifecycle order from one successful foreground run.

CheckpointRunner requests a finite background-task identifier before starting its synthetic two-second task. It handles an invalid identifier and captures a generation for both expiration and completion. Replacement/cancellation retires the generation and ends the identifier; old work cannot claim completion for a newer attempt. The task deliberately writes no durable file. The documented five-second callback budget is not a promise that its sleep, another Task, or a final save gets five guaranteed seconds.

Actual expiration cannot be scheduled precisely by the learner. Record it only if observed, and otherwise mark it pending. Durable drafts, account authentication, universal links, session-restoration activities, and protected-data recovery need additional fixtures. This is an ownership and acceptance lab, not a production migration or evidence that the learner has passed every checkpoint.

exercise.brief: Create a pending/observed evidence notebook for the four surfaces and add one bounded model-replacement, finish-animation, row-key, or restoration extension in a scratch copy.
steps: Build with the README command and run both shared-source host executables.
Choose one extension; define its owner, invalidation/terminal event, availability, and expected values.
Execute applicable UI scenarios on a functioning destination, or mark them pending if unavailable.
Record host assertions, build result, actual UI observations, and unresolved specialist gaps in separate rows.
Keep the company client and all existing course labs untouched.
acceptance: Host geometry/routes and macOS KVO assertions pass using the shared sources.
The standalone app builds at the declared deployment target; signing/runtime claims match actual evidence.
The selected extension has explicit failure and cancellation behavior.
At least one evidence row distinguishes source inspection from compile and runtime results.
Unexecuted VoiceOver, multiwindow, installed routing, or expiration checks remain pending.
exercise.solution:
A useful worked extension is replaceable observation because it exposes ownership without requiring device timing. In a scratch copy, invalidate and clear the current token, assign a new CounterRecord, then register .initial/.new on that record. Keep a diagnostic reference to the old record. After the new record starts at ten, mutating the old record must leave the display at ten; mutating the current record to eleven must show eleven. Weak capture prevents one ownership cycle, while token retirement stops obsolete registration.

The notebook should name the artifact and boundary for each result. The actual host checks establish seven logical geometry scenarios plus restoration/cold/warm routing policy and nine rejected URL forms; the separate KVO program establishes initial/new values and idempotent invalidation on macOS. The actual iOS target build establishes source/API/package correctness with its environment workaround. Neither result proves the replaceable-model UI extension, because that extension remains learner work.

For runtime rows record a destination, input sequence, observed action or state, and any interruption. A successful double tap should only add ten, Reset should resolve through the controller, and an empty overlay should not steal Increment. Layer Freeze and Finish should persist different model values. Larger text should update measured arrangement inputs; the RTL toggle asks SwiftUI to reflect unchanged logical positions while retaining logical identities. Native RTL behavior still needs observation. Validation should expose a reachable error with editing and assistive focus tracked independently.

For lifecycle rows, external Beta should beat stale Alpha restoration, invalid warm input should preserve the current selection, and an obsolete checkpoint should never end a replacement attempt. Do not save a draft only at termination or call a synthetic sleep durable work. If CoreSimulator remains unavailable, the notebook's UI rows stay pending and the next action is to run them on an available destination. The exercise defines checkable outcomes; it does not automatically record course completion.

quiz.question: What does a successful generic simulator build establish?
options: Compiled/linked/packaged SDK correctness for that target
Installed URL delivery and VoiceOver order
Measured frame deadlines on a physical device
quiz.explanation: A generic build produces a simulator app product without executing it. Runtime delivery, assistive traversal, and physical-device timing are independent evidence.

quiz.question: Why does the cache include baseline and row-break values?
options: They keep the same controller alive
They change arrangement without necessarily changing child count or identity
quiz.explanation: An unchanged child set can move rows or require different alignment extents. Cache validity must include the current geometry and key inputs.

quiz.question: A checkpoint's old expiration callback arrives after replacement. What should decide acceptance?
options: The attempt generation captured by that callback
quiz.explanation: A matching generation prevents an earlier expiration from retiring newer work. Ending a background identifier and protecting durable writes are still separate responsibilities.
